summary: Decompose 17 oversize Python source files into sub-packages following the canonical pattern in docs/guides/decomposition-pattern.md so the global 1500-line / 100KB file-size lint cap holds without grandfathering. The acceptance criterion is binary: scripts/file-size-allowlist.yaml `files:` map empties, every entry's source file lands under the cap, and the seam tables in orchestrator/CLAUDE.md, gateway/CLAUDE.md (and the new sandbox/CLAUDE.md + shared/CLAUDE.md per cq-2) carry concrete submodule layouts rather than TBD rows. This pipeline is the second-pass attempt — #2261 stalled after only the pattern + select_tests reference landed (#2335).

background.why_refresh: Six pipeline attempts on #2261 (v3 through v10) failed to land any follow-up decomposition slice after #2335. Files have grown 30-50% since the prior plan was written (pipelines.py: 16,401 -> 24,559 LOC; gateway.py: 9,890 -> 10,690 LOC; orch_cli.py: 3,537 -> 4,034 LOC). Cluster pre-allocations from the prior plan still match seams structurally but the larger files now require sub-sub-packages.

approaches_considered.name: Monolithic-per-file slices (prior #2261 shape)
approaches_considered.shape: One slice per oversize file (15-17 slices), each landing the entire decomposition in one PR. pipelines.py and gateway.py each as a single slice with internal task list.
pros: Each slice's PR review is a complete picture of one file's decomposition
cons: Prior plan tried this; six pipeline attempts (v3-v10) stalled with NO follow-up slices landing

pipelines.py at 24,559 LOC requires extracting 10 clusters + factoring a 2,935-LOC function; one BRC cycle cannot converge this — the prompt explicitly forbids slices that would require >3-4 commit-propose-revise cycles

approaches_considered.shape: Decompose pipelines.py via parallel children of a baseline slice: _prompt_building/, _pr_lifecycle/, _worktree_ops/, _concurrent_phase/, _run_loop/ as sibling sub-slices.
cons: The allowlist entry stays until ALL sub-slices land; the slice that drops the entry would depend on all siblings — forest violation (multi-parent)

serialized_chain_order would have to encode the chain anyway

approaches_considered.name: Chained sub-slices for outliers + parallel siblings for the 15 smaller files (RECOMMENDED)
approaches_considered.shape: Slice-1 (docs scaffolding root). Then: pipelines.py as 6 chained sub-slices (slice-2 baseline+small -> slice-3 _prompt_building -> slice-4 _pr_lifecycle -> slice-5 _worktree_ops -> slice-6 _concurrent_phase -> slice-7 _run_loop terminal). Gateway.py as 5 chained sub-slices (slice-8 baseline+small -> slice-9 _git_routes -> slice-10 _jira_routes -> slice-11 _confluence_routes+small -> slice-12 terminal). The other 15 files as one slice each, all siblings of slice-1.
pros: Each sub-slice converges in one BRC cycle (small enough that 1-2 commit-propose-revise iterations suffice)
Forest-valid (every slice has exactly one parent)
Chains serialise barrel mutation inside each outlier file, avoiding rebase storms
The 15 simpler files run in parallel (limited by EGG_ORCH_MAX_PARALLEL_SLICES=2 per pipeline), so wall-clock is bounded by the longer of the two chains (6 + small terminal vs 5 + small terminal)
The terminal sub-slice of each chain owns the allowlist drop + seam-table finalization — clean acceptance boundary
Docs prep up-front (slice-1) means downstream slices don't need to do scaffolding work
cons: 27 slices total — large slice count vs prior plan's 15
Outlier chains serialise wall-clock: pipelines.py decomposition is ~6 sequential PRs
approaches_considered.verdict: RECOMMENDED — this is the only shape that respects the forest constraint AND the 'no slice requires >3-4 BRC cycles' rule.

approaches_considered.name: Inline cq-2/cq-4/cq-5/cq-6 doc work into each per-file slice (no separate docs slice)
approaches_considered.shape: No slice-1. Each per-file slice owns the doc updates relevant to its file (e.g. the pipelines.py terminal slice updates pipelines.py's seam-table row; the docs-pattern relaxation lands in whichever slice touches docs/guides/decomposition-pattern.md first).
cons: The docs/guides/decomposition-pattern.md update (cq-4) and #2261->#2817 reference fixup (cq-6) have no natural single owner among the per-file slices; first-touch is arbitrary and reviewers can't predict where to look
Creating sandbox/CLAUDE.md (cq-2) and shared/CLAUDE.md (cq-2) likewise has no natural per-file owner — those files don't exist yet so they're not in any per-file slice's scope
Without an up-front docs slice, allowlist-comment fixes (cq-5) end up duplicated across slices, increasing conflict surface
approaches_considered.verdict: REJECTED — fragmenting docs across slices creates coordination overhead with no compensating benefit.

recommended_approach.name: Chained sub-slices for outliers + parallel siblings for smaller files, with up-front docs slice

technical_decisions.decision: Up-front docs-only slice (slice-1) absorbs cq-2, cq-4, cq-5, cq-6 doc work
technical_decisions.rationale: cq-6 explicitly delegates packaging to the planner ('separate docs-only slice up-front', 'inlined per slice', or 'hybrid'). Up-front is the most coherent because cq-4 (pattern doc relaxation) and cq-2 (new sandbox/shared CLAUDE.md seam tables) have no natural per-file owner.
technical_decisions.trade_off: Adds 1 extra slice; in exchange every per-file slice's task list shrinks (no doc-scaffolding work to coordinate).

technical_decisions.decision: Chained sub-slices for pipelines.py (6) and gateway.py (5)
technical_decisions.rationale: Forest constraint forbids multi-parent slices. Parallel sub-slices that all touch the barrel + allowlist would either violate the forest (if the terminal depended on all) or create rebase storms (if they all landed against the same parent simultaneously). Chained sub-slices serialise barrel mutation cleanly; the only rebase conflict surface is scripts/file-size-allowlist.yaml, which has a documented recipe.
technical_decisions.trade_off: Wall-clock floor of 7 sequential merges (slice-1 -> slice-7); smaller files complete in parallel inside that window.

technical_decisions.decision: Outlier terminal sub-slice owns the allowlist drop + final seam-table row
technical_decisions.rationale: scripts/file-size-allowlist.yaml's lint enforces a RATCHET — each PR touching an allowlisted entry must reduce its size. Intermediate sub-slices reduce size (each extracts a cluster) but the entry only comes out once the file drops below 1500 lines. Likewise the seam-table row in orchestrator/CLAUDE.md is TBD until the FULL submodule layout is known; intermediate sub-slices may update with partial info but the terminal one writes the concrete final layout.
technical_decisions.trade_off: Intermediate sub-slices need to keep the allowlist entry intact even though they shrink the file (no risk to lint as long as size strictly decreases).

technical_decisions.decision: Cluster names in the architect output are GUIDANCE, not prescriptions
technical_decisions.rationale: The architect prompt says 'right-size slices for a single BRC cycle' but does not say the architect prescribes the final submodule shape. The implementing producer for each slice reads the file and makes the final cluster boundary call. The architect's job is to verify each slice fits in the cap with SOME reasonable split, not to dictate the exact submodule names.
technical_decisions.trade_off: Slight risk that an implementing agent splits differently from the scaffold; reviewer_code is empowered to NACK on slice_size if the producer's choices don't fit.

technical_decisions.decision: monitor.py pre-split into 2-slice chain (slice-22 prep + slice-23 extract); phases.py flagged needs-deeper-inspection but stays single-slice
technical_decisions.rationale: monitor.py's 885-LOC write_health_summary method (lines 198-1083) must be broken up BEFORE submodule cluster boundaries can be named — the prep work alone is ~3 named helper extractions plus 5 submodule extractions on top, which is 8+ distinct named code-motion changes plus two different review attention surfaces (prep-refactor vs cluster-extract) in one PR. Per the §11 slice_size rubric, this is too much for one BRC cycle. The v1 architect output had this as a single slice with td-7 noting the contingency; reviewer_plan correctly NACKed and the v2 scaffold pre-splits into slice-22 (in-place breakup, allowlist stays) + slice-23 (submodule extract, allowlist drops). phases.py's 540-LOC advance_phase route body dominates that file; the implementing agent must find its internal seams, but the slice has only one mega-function (not a 5-cluster extraction following it), so single-slice convergence is achievable.
technical_decisions.trade_off: One extra slice (28 total vs 27). In exchange, reviewer attention is focused on one risk profile at a time and the reactive NACK fallback no longer adds wall-clock pressure mid-cycle.

technical_decisions.decision: phases.py decomposition preserves lazy in-function imports
technical_decisions.rationale: phases.py uses `from routes.pipelines import _foo` inside route bodies (not at module level) specifically to break the import cycle with pipelines.py. Carving out _advance.py / _complete.py / etc. submodules must preserve this — hoisting to module-level imports reintroduces the cycle and breaks orchestrator boot.
technical_decisions.trade_off: Per-submodule code is slightly uglier (each route body re-imports the pipelines.py helpers it needs); cycle-safety is the dominant constraint.

technical_decisions.decision: peer_consensus.py stays single-slice; the implementing agent decides whether _run_invariant_checks extracts to _invariants.py or stays as a private method on the class
technical_decisions.rationale: peer_consensus.py is HARD but the complexity is localized to one method placement decision (whether _run_invariant_checks extracts or stays on the class), NOT an 885-LOC mega-method that needs in-place breakup. The implementing agent can decide on inspection. If extraction creates circular-import problems with the per-handler clusters, the safe fallback is keeping _run_invariant_checks on the class itself in __init__.py. Within one slice's scope. monitor.py's case was different and got pre-split into slice-22+23 per td-5.

technical_decisions.decision: Pre-allocated TBD placeholders in slice-2 must be VALID PYTHON (not import-of-non-existent-module)
technical_decisions.rationale: Slice-2 pre-allocates 5 sub-sub-package TBD entries in pipelines/__init__.py for downstream chained sub-slices to fill. The __init__.py is loaded at orchestrator boot time; an ImportError of a non-existent submodule would brick the pipeline. Placeholders must be docstring comments or `pass` statements, NOT `from ._prompt_building import *`.

technical_decisions.decision: External-importer audit grep must be UN-ANCHORED across the whole repo to catch in-function lazy importers
technical_decisions.rationale: mcp_tools.py uses the double-prefix form `from orchestrator.routes.pipelines import _read_phase_draft` inside function bodies (lazy import). A module-level-anchored grep misses this. The slice-2 description mandates `git grep -nE 'from (orchestrator\.)?routes\.pipelines' -- '*.py'` (un-anchored regex) to catch both single- and double-prefix forms and both module-level and in-function importers.
